status_summary: On 2025-09-19 DOL launched Project Firewall, an H-1B enforcement initiative under which the Secretary of Labor personally certifies the start of investigations where there is reasonable cause to suspect noncompliance, led by the Office of Immigration Policy, ETA and the Wage and Hour Division; violations can lead to back wages, civil penalties or debarment from the H-1B program. DOL debarment lists show H-1B debarments with periods beginning from 2025-05-12 to 2026-09-24 and dozens of H-2A, H-2B and permanent certification debarments beginning in 2025 and 2026. The lists do not show whether debarments became faster, the release does not mention exclusion from federal contracts, and action on the 2020 Inspector General recommendations was not found.

timeline.event: DOL announces Project Firewall: H-1B enforcement initiative with Secretary-certified investigations and possible debarment (Release No. 25-1476-NAT).
H-1B debarment period begins for the latest of six entries on the Wage and Hour Division list (earliest start 2025-05-12); the page was last updated 2026-09-30.
timeline.source: Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division

title: Step up visa fraud investigations and debarments of abusive foreign labor employers
uncertainties: The release and both debarment lists were fetched and re-read in review. The OFLC list is undated and has 54 entries (2 permanent certification, 25 H-2A, 27 H-2B), with debarment start dates in 2025 and 2026; the start date of a debarment period is not necessarily the date of the final order, and the lists show only current debarments, so earlier periods cannot be compared to judge speed. The Inspector General's 2020 report and any DOL response were not located. A Federal Register API search of ETA documents for debarment returned no rules specific to debarment. Searches run: three WebSearches by the researcher (debarment announcements, Project Firewall, debarment list) and fetches; no WebSearch in review. Press coverage of H-1B debarments was seen in results but not cited. Project Firewall targets H-1B compliance generally, which overlaps with but is not the same as visa fraud.
